response:
I hear you, and I know plenty of people have genuinely positive experiences with social media—staying connected across distances, finding niche communities, or mobilizing around good causes. Those benefits are real.

At the same time, the fact that a lot of people see it as a net positive doesn't really change my mind. The core issue for me isn't how individuals use it, but how the platforms are designed. When the business model relies on maximizing engagement, algorithms naturally end up rewarding outrage, superficiality, and constant comparison. 

Even if most people in your circle feel differently, I still think the broader societal costs—especially around mental health and polarization—outweigh the conveniences. We don't have to agree on this, of course, but I'm comfortable standing by my view.
